_note: Mission types, module sites, zones and contract settings (wave 4 W10; wave 4B part 2). The first four mission types are Captain's first four from the mission brainstorm (docs/mission_brainstorm.md): raid, HVT capture, hostage rescue and intel grab; mission variety (2026-10-15, docs/missions.md) adds convoy ambush, hold the line, downed crew rescue, sabotage and recon. MissionRegistry reads them (MissionRegistry.register_type adds more at runtime). Every number in settings, every time limit and every pay figure is Proposed and tunable.
_mission_types: A type names the module types it can play in ("modules"); a contract picks one of the zone's modules of those types as its target, and each objective template names a site of that module ("site": one name, or a list to pick from). An optional objective whose site the module lacks is left out. In "text", {name} is the site's (or the person's) name and {module} the module's. "time_limit_min" (Proposed: about twice the expected completion time, forgiving) fails the required objectives still open when it runs out.

mission_types.name: Raid
mission_types.brief: Hostiles keep a weapons cache or an AA gun at a site in the zone. Destroy it: grenades break crates, a steel gun takes a placed breaching charge (base shop).

objectives.text: Bonus: leave no fighter standing in the {module}

mission_types.name: HVT capture
mission_types.brief: A hostile HVT is at a site in the zone. Take them alive and bring them to extraction: they run, shout and fight back until cornered or zip-cuffed. Cuffs from the base shop keep them; an uncuffed captive left alone bolts, so someone stays close. They bleed out like anyone. On the clock.

objectives.text: Capture {name} and bring them to extraction alive

mission_types.name: Hostage rescue
mission_types.brief: A hostage is held at a site in the zone. Find them and bring them out alive: they follow the squad once found. On the clock.

objectives.text: Find {name} and bring them out alive
Bonus: leave no guard standing in the {module}

mission_types.name: Intel grab
mission_types.brief: Intel sits at a site in the zone: a laptop or a hard case. Carry it out; it only counts once it's out.

objectives.text: Recover the {name} and carry it out

mission_types.name: Convoy ambush
mission_types.brief: An enemy convoy (a cargo truck or two with armed escorts) drives a road across the zone. Set up on the route, stop it (destroy the cargo trucks, or kill the drivers and disable them) before it leaves the far end, then seize the cargo crate. It rolls about 7-10 minutes after insertion, so the squad needs to be in position.

mission_types.name: Hold the line
mission_types.brief: The client needs a position held while their people pull out. Hold it for the time given against attack waves from several directions. The clock runs while someone of ours stands in it; if nobody holds it and the enemy walks in, it falls and the contract fails. Extract once the time is up.

mission_types.name: Downed crew rescue
mission_types.brief: A Black Hawk went down in open ground. Its crew (2-4) is alive, some wounded: a broken leg means a carry. Find the wreck, treat and carry them and get them to extraction. Hostiles converge on the crash site in waves, starting a few minutes in. One loss is acceptable; bringing out all of them earns a bonus.

mission_types.name: Sabotage
mission_types.brief: Hit what the enemy fights with, not the fighters: its fuel store, its vehicle park or its radio mast at a site in the zone. Steel fuel drums and a steel mast shrug off grenades: bring breaching charges (base shop) and set one on the target; a park needs one on each vehicle (it counts once it burns or can't drive). Bonus pay for an AA gun there too, and for getting in and out without a hostile ever getting eyes on the squad.
mission_types._objectives: The target is one of the module's sabotage sites ("fuel", "park", "mast"; a module has at least one). A site's own "kind" stands in for the template's (a vehicle park: destroy_vehicles, MissionScenario parks them there). Mission variety, 2026-10-20 (docs/missions.md). A bridge waits for roads that cross water.

objectives.text: Bonus: in and out unseen (no hostile in contact with the squad)

mission_types.name: Recon
mission_types.brief: Observe several enemy sites in the zone: get within sight of each and stay a few seconds with a clear line of sight (no need to engage). Bonus pay if the squad is never spotted.

mission_types.name: Client escort
mission_types.brief: Personal security detail. A client (an engineer, an aid official or a journalist) is waiting at a site in the zone. Meet them and get them to extraction alive: they follow the squad once met. Word has got out: expect an ambush set on the way to the extraction and more fighters coming after the client as you go. Bonus pay if the client comes out without a scratch.

mission_types.name: Supply line
mission_types.brief: Hostiles move weapons along a line of caches across neighbouring zones. Destroy the cache here and the one in the next zone over: walk on through the crossing between them (docs/linked_zones.md LZ-7).

mission_types.name: Manhunt
mission_types.brief: A hostile HVT has moved on. His people left intel behind at a site in this zone saying where: grab it, then follow him into the zone next door (walk on through the crossing between them), take him alive and bring him to extraction there (docs/linked_zones.md LZ-7).

objectives.text: Recover the {name}: it says where he went

leg_objectives.text: Capture {name} and bring them to extraction alive

mission_types.name: Convoy chase
mission_types.brief: An enemy convoy drives across the zone and on into the next. Stop it here for a bonus; if it gets away, chase it through the crossing and stop it there (already rolling when you arrive). Stopped here, the job is done (docs/linked_zones.md LZ-7).

mission_types.name: Locals: the checkpoint
mission_types.brief: A checkpoint near the village taxes everyone who passes, and worse. The villagers want it gone: clear it. They pay what they can, and they'll remember.

mission_types.name: Locals: a missing villager
mission_types.brief: Gunmen took a villager. Find them where they're held and bring them out alive. The family pays what it can; the village won't forget it.

mission_types.name: Locals: the stolen stores
mission_types.brief: Gunmen took the village's stores and keep them at a site nearby. Destroy what they keep there so they can't sell it back to them.

mission_types.name: Forward observer
mission_types._about: Fire support, 2026-10-20 (FireSupport, ObserverMission): get eyes on the target area, bring the guns onto each target, stay unseen. Paid by the targets the guns destroy: the first is the job, each other a bonus. Proposed numbers.
mission_types.brief: The client wants a site hit without anyone setting foot on it. Get eyes on the target area, then call the mortars or the battery (Support > Fire support) onto the vehicles and weapon positions there: adjust onto each one, fire for effect. Paid per target the guns destroy; one put out of action any other way doesn't count. Stay unseen for a bonus. The rounds are paid from the support budget, then cash.

_modules: Sites per module type, in metres from the module's origin on the ground (the zone module types of ZoneModules; the compound as CompoundLevel builds it). rect [x, z, w, d] (clear an area), pos [x, y, z], box [[x, y, z], [x, y, z]] (a cache: "voxels" is its solid count on the pristine module, "auto" counts it from the module's boxes). "place": an intel item the mission puts there; "items"/"tags": what counts as carried out; "hvt" + "person": a person the mission puts there (side hostile: an HVT to capture, friendly: a hostage); "of_hvt": an item the HVT of that site carries. "civilians": people going about their day there while a contract runs in the zone ("routine": points they walk between). Sabotage targets (2026-10-20): "fuel" (a fuel store, a box like a cache), "mast" (the comms site's mast) and "park" (a vehicle park: "vehicles" models parked side by side "spacing_m" apart about "pos", facing "yaw_deg"; MissionScenario parks them when the contract goes live); a site's "kind" stands in for its objective template's.

cache.name: weapons cache
cache._voxels: solid voxels in the box on the pristine module (the crate stack: three 1 m crates); the destroyed share is measured against this

fuel.name: fuel store
fuel._note: the two generators and their fuel drums (steel: it takes a placed charge)

town.name: town
town._note: A generated town (ZoneModules "town#<seed>"): its sites and civilians come from its own buildings (ZoneModules.town_sites, BuildingGen.town).

mast.name: radio mast
mast._note: the cache site's mast, by its sabotage name

_names: The people a mission puts in a zone have real names (Names.mission_person): HVTs from the target faction's nation (factions.json "nation"), hostages from mixed nationalities, civilians from the region's own people (regions' "nation").
_zones: Terror groups and the living war (2026-10-20, docs/terror_groups.md): "controller" is who holds a zone at a campaign's start (WorldSites seeds from it; the faction war moves it), "assets" what it's worth fighting for (a faction's "war_wants" weighs them) and "home" the factions whose home ground it is. Every zone is a generated world-scale zone (ZoneDef.generate from "def": seed, size_m, types, count), the same layout every visit so the persistent world holds (zone saves are per zone id). "modules" (the module types it holds) is filled in from the layout. Contract zones are 2-4 km² (1536 m or 1920 m a side). Hot zones ("layout": "hot": ZoneDef.generate_hot) are 16 km², a 4096 m square (Captain, 2026-10-12): an HQ, outposts, road checkpoints, QRF bases, a comms site and villages.

zones.name: FOB Halberd
zones._note: D7 (docs/combined_arms.md 7.3): the US forces' base in the theatre, held from day 1, never falls (cant_fall: sieged at most, like a faction's last zone). "map_cell" puts it on the region grid by hand ([column, row] in its region's block), north of Cove outpost, without moving any other zone. No contracts are offered in it (kind allied_fob); every site's garrison is American (UsField). D8 stages the company here.

_story: The campaign's story (docs/story.md, Story): its acts, the handmade story contracts (an existing type with its own name, brief and objectives; "after" the ones done before it and the "clues" it needs; "clue" what its intel says and its evidence worth; the liaison's "line_offer" and "line_done") and the faction arcs. An act after the first opens at its "evidence" count (Captain 2026-10-20: both a clue per contract and the count between acts; the mastermind is a consortium, four acts, act 1's four beats with the FOB after). Act 1 is built; acts 2-4 and the arcs are stubs ("built": false, "stub": true) to fill in. Names, lines and numbers Proposed.

acts.name: The coast
acts.summary: From the LHD, against Black Ridge: their weapons aren't smuggled, a contractor ships them, and the contractor is the Vantage Group.

acts.name: Ashore
acts.summary: From the FOB: Vantage arms Black Ridge and the Eastern Concord's officers alike, paid through Halden Maritime. Vantage hit teams start coming.

acts.name: The money
acts.summary: Who owns Halden: a consortium that profits from the war going on. Vantage comes for the company at the FOB.

acts.name: The company's own
acts.summary: The allies won't move against the backers; the company becomes its own faction (the late-game player faction).

contracts.name: Paper trail
contracts.brief: Meridian's convoys keep running into Black Ridge fighters carrying new rifles, still in the grease. Somebody is supplying them. Get into the site, take their laptop and carry it out: we want to know who ships their weapons.

objectives.text: Recover the {name}: who ships their weapons?

clue.text: Black Ridge's laptop: their rifles came in sealed crates with a logistics contractor's shipping marks. Not smuggled: delivered.

contracts.line_offer: Radio, client liaison: Meridian has a job for you, and it's more than a job. Black Ridge is getting new weapons from somewhere. Find out where. It's on the board.
contracts.line_done: Radio, client liaison: Crates with a contractor's marks. Somebody's shipping guns to these people on a manifest. Their quartermaster will know who.

contracts.name: The quartermaster
contracts.brief: Black Ridge's quartermaster signs for every crate. He has moved on, but his people left papers behind saying where. Take them, follow him into the next zone (walk on through the crossing between them) and bring him out alive. He's no use to us dead.

objectives.text: Recover the {name}: it says where the quartermaster went

leg_objectives.text: Capture {name}, Black Ridge's quartermaster, and bring them to extraction alive

clue.text: The quartermaster, questioned: he paid for the crates into an account in the Vantage Group's name.

contracts.line_offer: Radio, client liaison: Their quartermaster signs for the crates, and he's on the move. Bring him in alive. It's on the board.
contracts.line_done: Radio, client liaison: He talked. The money went to Vantage, the outfit that's been racing you to sites. I want proof before Meridian says it out loud.

contracts.name: The crates
contracts.brief: The quartermaster named the caches the crates go to, here and in the next zone over. Destroy both, and bring out the waybills from the first: they say who drove the crates in. Walk on through the crossing between the zones.

clue.text: The waybills: the crates came in convoys under Vantage Group escort, signed off by one of their team leaders.

contracts.line_offer: Radio, client liaison: The quartermaster gave us his caches. Burn them, and get me the waybills. It's on the board.
contracts.line_done: Radio, client liaison: Vantage escorts. So it's them. One of their teams is handing a delivery over right now. Get me their ledger.

contracts.name: Vantage point
contracts.brief: A Vantage Group team is handing a weapons delivery over to Black Ridge at a site in this zone. They're professionals, not militia: expect good kit. Destroy the delivery and bring out their team leader's ledger.

objectives.text: Destroy the {name} Vantage is handing over

clue.text: The Vantage ledger: Vantage pays Black Ridge's commanders to keep fighting, and its own pay comes through a shipping firm, Halden Maritime.

contracts.line_offer: Radio, client liaison: Vantage is handing a delivery over to Black Ridge. Hit it and bring me their ledger. It's on the board.
contracts.line_done: Radio, client liaison: Vantage is paying Black Ridge to keep this war going, and somebody pays Vantage through Halden Maritime. This is bigger than Meridian's convoys.

contracts.name: Halden's manifests
contracts.brief: Stub (act 2): Halden Maritime's shipping office ashore. To write.

arcs.name: Company man
arcs.summary: A Meridian manager has been signing Vantage's escort contracts. Expose him or keep it quiet for a price.

arcs.name: Salvage rights
arcs.summary: The Union's boats see every ship that comes in. Protect a salvage job; they trade what they know of Halden's shipping.

arcs.name: Liaison
arcs.summary: Joint operations with the allies: a downed crew, a defend-and-hold. They share what they have on Vantage, and later won't act on it.

settings._economy_2026_10_20: Economy overhaul (docs/economy_proposal_2026-10-20.md, built 2026-10-20): pay about a third lower (difficulty_pay), hot zones keep their better rate (hot_zone_pay_mult 1.4: the overhaul's cut to 1.0 was undone the same day, when hot zones stopped handing out 3-6 contracts on arrival), the no-civilians bonus halved (clean_bonus_share 0.05), intel sells for its own intel_value x intel_sale_mult (not a flat price), and a hot zone's radio contracts pay nothing up front (all on completion); a hot zone goes in on the contracts taken for it, no top-up on arrival. Wages and upkeep are charged every day (Economy.advance_days).
settings._clawback_terms: Captain 2026-10-11: each contract states what happens to the advance if it is voided: none (keep it all), prorated (keep the share of required objectives done) or full (give it all back). Strict clients use full, shady ones none but pay less (pay_mult). Fixers are shady (none), the safe low-risk job strict (full); the rest are rolled by weight. Weights and pay_mult are Proposed.
settings._charges: Breaching charges (placed like Arma Reforger: a ghost on any surface, committed where it sits; one on a person or a vehicle rides along with it). The fuse runs from placing; a cache or AA objective counts as destroyed when a charge goes off within charge_kill_m of its box. Proposed.
settings._reinforcement: Reinforcements sized from the contract's true force (Contracts.reinforcement_tuning): the first wave comes at the first value for a 1-rated contract down to the second for a 5, max_pairs likewise; living hostiles are capped at the true enemy count plus alive_extra, at most alive_max; the waves' skill starts at the true quality. Proposed.
